column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|09-03|1530|Ιβάν Δ΄|Ivan IV|Ivan IV, known as "the Terrible", was the first to be crowned Tsar of Russia, in 1547. He extended the state towards the east and the Volga, but his reign remained known for its severity and brutality. He died in 1584.

bio|09-03|1658|Όλιβερ Κρόμγουελ|Oliver Cromwell|Oliver Cromwell was an English soldier and politician. He led the Parliamentary army in the Civil War and, after the execution of Charles I, became Lord Protector of England. He died in 1658.
bio|09-03|1875|Φερντινάντ Πόρσε|Ferdinand Porsche|Ferdinand Porsche was an Austrian automotive engineer. He designed the Volkswagen "Beetle" and founded the Porsche company. He died in 1951.

bio|09-03|1877|Αδόλφος Θιέρσος|Adolphe Thiers|Adolphe Thiers was a French politician and historian. He was the first president of the Third French Republic and suppressed the Paris Commune in 1871. He died in 1877.

bio|09-03|1883|Ιβάν Τουργκένιεφ|Ivan Turgenev|Ivan Turgenev was a Russian writer. He wrote the novels "Fathers and Sons" and "A Month in the Country" and lived for many years in France and Germany. He died in 1883.

bio|09-03|1905|Καρλ Ντέιβιντ Άντερσον|Carl David Anderson|Carl David Anderson was an American physicist. He discovered the positron, the antiparticle of the electron, and in 1936 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Victor Hess. He died in 1991.

bio|09-03|1936|Ζιν Ελ Αμπιντίν Μπεν Άλι|Zine El Abidine Ben Ali|Zine El Abidine Ben Ali was president of Tunisia from 1987 to 2011, when he was overthrown after protests that began the Arab Spring. He fled to Saudi Arabia and died in 2019.

bio|09-03|1947|Μάριο Ντράγκι|Mario Draghi|Mario Draghi is an Italian economist and banker. He was president of the European Central Bank from 2011 to 2019 and prime minister of Italy from 2021 to 2022.
bio|09-03|2012|Μάικλ Κλαρκ Ντάνκαν|Michael Clarke Duncan|Michael Clarke Duncan was an American actor. He was nominated for an Oscar for his role in the film "The Green Mile". He died in 2012.

bio|09-04|1768|Φρανσουά-Ρενέ ντε Σατωμπριάν|François-René de Chateaubriand|François-René de Chateaubriand was a French writer and diplomat, a forerunner of Romanticism in France. He wrote "Memoirs from Beyond the Grave". He died in 1848.
bio|09-04|1824|Άντον Μπρούκνερ|Anton Bruckner|Anton Bruckner was an Austrian composer and organist. He wrote nine large symphonies and religious works with a majestic style. He died in 1896.

bio|09-04|1896|Αντονέν Αρτώ|Antonin Artaud|Antonin Artaud was a French playwright and theorist. In the book "The Theatre and Its Double" he proposed the "theatre of cruelty", which influenced modern theatre. He died in 1948.
bio|09-04|1907|Έντβαρντ Γκρηγκ|Edvard Grieg|Edvard Grieg was a Norwegian composer of Romanticism. He wrote the music for Ibsen's "Peer Gynt" and the Piano Concerto in A minor. He died in 1907.

bio|09-04|1965|Άλμπερτ Σβάιτσερ|Albert Schweitzer|Albert Schweitzer was a German doctor, theologian and musician. He founded a hospital at Lambaréné in Gabon, and in 1952 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. He died in 1965.
bio|09-04|1981|Μπιγιονσέ|Beyoncé|Beyoncé is an American singer and songwriter. She began with Destiny's Child and has won many Grammy awards as a solo artist, with hits such as "Crazy in Love".
bio|09-04|1985|Ραούλ Αλμπιόλ|Raúl Albiol|Raúl Albiol is a Spanish footballer who plays as a defender. He played for Valencia, Real Madrid and Napoli, and he won the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012.
bio|09-04|1989|Ζωρζ Σιμενόν|Georges Simenon|Georges Simenon was a Belgian writer. He created Inspector Maigret and wrote hundreds of detective novels. He died in 1989.

bio|09-04|2006|Στιβ Άιρβιν|Steve Irwin|Steve Irwin was an Australian naturalist and television presenter, known as "the Crocodile Hunter". He died in 2006 from a stingray bite while filming a documentary on the Great Barrier Reef.

bio|09-05|1568|Τομάζο Καμπανέλα|Tommaso Campanella|Tommaso Campanella was an Italian philosopher and monk. He wrote "The City of the Sun", a utopia, and was imprisoned for years for his opposition to Spanish rule in Naples. He died in 1639.

bio|09-05|1638|Λουδοβίκος ΙΔ΄|Louis XIV|Louis XIV was born in 1638 and became King of France in 1643, as a child. He remained on the throne until 1715 and became known as the "Sun King". He built the Palace of Versailles.

bio|09-05|1774|Κάσπαρ Ντάβιντ Φρίντριχ|Caspar David Friedrich|Caspar David Friedrich was a German Romantic painter. He became known for his landscapes with fog and solitary figures, such as "Wanderer above the Sea of Fog". He died in 1840.
bio|09-05|1857|Ογκίστ Κοντ|Auguste Comte|Auguste Comte was a French philosopher. He is considered the founder of positivism and of sociology as a science. He died in 1857.

bio|09-05|1902|Ρούντολφ Βίρχοβ|Rudolf Virchow|Rudolf Virchow was a German physician and politician. He is regarded as the father of pathological anatomy and formulated that every cell comes from another cell. He died in 1902.

bio|09-05|1906|Λούντβιχ Μπόλτσμαν|Ludwig Boltzmann|Ludwig Boltzmann was an Austrian physicist. He developed statistical mechanics and interpreted entropy on the basis of probability. He took his own life in 1906.

bio|09-05|1946|Φρέντι Μέρκιουρι|Freddie Mercury|Freddie Mercury was born in Zanzibar and was the singer of Queen. He wrote hits such as "Bohemian Rhapsody" and "Somebody to Love". He died in 1991 from complications of AIDS.
bio|09-05|1951|Μάικλ Κίτον|Michael Keaton|Michael Keaton is an American actor. He became known as Batman in the films of Tim Burton and appeared in "Birdman", for which he was nominated for an Oscar.

bio|09-05|1997|Μητέρα Τερέζα|Mother Teresa|Mother Teresa died on 5 September 1997 in Calcutta. She was a Catholic nun of Albanian origin, born in Skopje, and she founded the Missionaries of Charity. The Catholic Church declared her a saint in 2016.

bio|09-06|1757|Ζιλμπέρ ντυ Μοτιέ ντε Λα Φαγιέτ|Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette|The Marquis de Lafayette was a French officer. He fought alongside the Americans in the War of Independence and took part in the early phases of the French Revolution. He died in 1834.
bio|09-06|1766|Τζον Ντάλτον|John Dalton|John Dalton was an English chemist and physicist. He formulated the atomic theory of matter and described his own colour blindness. He died in 1844.

bio|09-06|1892|Έντουαρντ Βίκτορ Άπλετον|Edward Victor Appleton|Edward Victor Appleton was an English physicist. He proved the existence of the ionosphere, which helps the propagation of radio waves, and in 1947 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1965.
bio|09-06|1907|Συλί Προυντόμ|Sully Prudhomme|Sully Prudhomme was a French poet of the Parnassian movement. In 1901 he became the first to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1907.

bio|09-06|1943|Ρότζερ Γουώτερς|Roger Waters|Roger Waters is an English singer and bassist. He was the main lyricist of Pink Floyd and the creator of the albums "The Wall" and "The Dark Side of the Moon".
bio|09-06|1963|Γκερτ Βίλντερς|Geert Wilders|Geert Wilders is a Dutch far-right politician. He founded the Party for Freedom in 2006 and is known for his anti-Islamic positions.

bio|09-06|1998|Ακίρα Κουροσάβα|Akira Kurosawa|Akira Kurosawa was a Japanese director and one of the greatest in the history of cinema. He directed "Rashomon", "Seven Samurai" and "Ran". He died in 1998.

bio|09-06|2007|Λουτσιάνο Παβαρότι|Luciano Pavarotti|Luciano Pavarotti was an Italian tenor, one of the best-known in opera. He became known to the wider public with "The Three Tenors". He died in 2007.
bio|09-06|2021|Ζαν Πολ Μπελμοντό|Jean-Paul Belmondo|Jean-Paul Belmondo was a French actor. He became a symbol of the French New Wave with Godard's film "Breathless". He died in 2021.

bio|09-07|1533|Ελισάβετ Α΄|Elizabeth I|Elizabeth I was Queen of England from 1558 to 1603. Her era, the "Elizabethan" age, flourished in literature and theatre, and England defeated the Spanish Armada in 1588.

bio|09-07|1566|Σουλεϊμάν Α΄ ο Μεγαλοπρεπής|Suleiman I the Magnificent|Suleiman I the Magnificent was Ottoman sultan from 1520 to 1566. He took Belgrade and Rhodes, won the Battle of Mohács and besieged Vienna. He died during a campaign in Hungary.
bio|09-07|1911|Τόντορ Ζίβκοβ|Todor Zhivkov|Todor Zhivkov was a Bulgarian communist politician. He led Bulgaria from 1954 to 1989, when he was forced to resign. He died in 1998.
bio|09-07|1930|Βαλδουίνος|Baudouin|Baudouin was King of the Belgians from 1951 to 1993. He was deeply religious and was beloved by the people. He died in 1993.

bio|09-07|1936|Μπάντι Χόλι|Buddy Holly|Buddy Holly was an American singer and songwriter, a pioneer of rock and roll. He wrote hits such as "That'll Be the Day". He was killed in a plane crash in 1959, at the age of 22.
bio|09-07|1962|Κάρεν Μπλίξεν|Karen Blixen|Karen Blixen was a Danish writer who used the pen name Isak Dinesen. She wrote "Out of Africa" about her years in Kenya. She died in 1962.

bio|09-07|1991|Έντουιν Μ. ΜακΜίλαν|Edwin M. McMillan|Edwin M. McMillan was an American physicist. He discovered neptunium and in 1951 he shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Glenn Seaborg. He died in 1991.

bio|09-07|1997|Μομπούτου Σέσε Σέκο|Mobutu Sese Seko|Mobutu Sese Seko was the leader of Zaire, today the Democratic Republic of the Congo, from 1965 to 1997. He ruled as a dictator, and the country experienced great corruption. He was overthrown and died in Morocco.

bio|09-08|1157|Ριχάρδος ο Λεοντόκαρδος|Richard the Lionheart|Richard the Lionheart was King of England from 1189 to 1199. He took part in the Third Crusade and entered Cyprus in 1191. He died in 1199.

bio|09-08|1830|Φρεντερίκ Μιστράλ|Frédéric Mistral|Frédéric Mistral was a French poet who wrote in Provençal. He wrote the epic "Mirèio" and in 1904 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1914.
bio|09-08|1841|Αντονίν Ντβόρζακ|Antonín Dvořák|Antonín Dvořák was a Czech composer. He wrote the "New World" Symphony and the "Slavonic Dances". He died in 1904.

bio|09-08|1925|Πίτερ Σέλλερς|Peter Sellers|Peter Sellers was an English actor and comedian. He became known as Inspector Clouseau in the "Pink Panther" series and in "Dr. Strangelove". He died in 1980.

bio|09-08|1941|Μπέρνι Σάντερς|Bernie Sanders|Bernie Sanders is an American politician, a senator from Vermont. He describes himself as a democratic socialist and unsuccessfully sought the Democratic nomination for the presidency in 2016 and 2020.

bio|09-08|1949|Ρίχαρντ Στράους|Richard Strauss|Richard Strauss was a German composer and conductor. He wrote symphonic poems, such as "Thus Spoke Zarathustra", and operas, such as "Salome" and "Der Rosenkavalier". He died in 1949.

bio|09-08|1981|Χίντεκι Γιουκάβα|Hideki Yukawa|Hideki Yukawa was a Japanese physicist. He predicted the existence of the meson, and in 1949 he became the first Japanese to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1981.
bio|09-08|2003|Λένι Ρίφενσταλ|Leni Riefenstahl|Leni Riefenstahl died in 2003, at the age of 101. She was a German director and photographer, known for the propaganda films she made for the Nazis.

bio|09-08|2022|Βασίλισσα Ελισάβετ Β'|Elizabeth II|Elizabeth II was Queen of the United Kingdom from 1952. She reigned for 70 years, the longest reign in British history. She died on 8 September 2022 at Balmoral, and she was succeeded by her son, Charles III.

bio|09-09|1087|Γουλιέλμος Α΄|William I|William I, known as William the Conqueror, was Duke of Normandy and King of England from 1066, when he won the Battle of Hastings. He died in 1087, after a fall from his horse during a campaign in France.

bio|09-09|1569|Πίτερ Μπρίγκελ ο πρεσβύτερος|Pieter Bruegel the Elder|Pieter Bruegel the Elder was a Flemish painter. He painted scenes of rural life, such as "Winter" and "The Tower of Babel", and the proverbs of his time. He died in 1569.

bio|09-09|1585|Αρμάν Ζαν ντυ Πλεσσί ντε Ρισελιέ|Armand Jean du Plessis, Cardinal Richelieu|Cardinal Richelieu was a French politician. As prime minister to Louis XIII he strengthened royal power and founded the French Academy. He died in 1642.

bio|09-09|1828|Λέων Τολστόι|Leo Tolstoy|Leo Tolstoy was a Russian writer. He wrote the novels "War and Peace" and "Anna Karenina". In his last years he developed a Christian philosophy of non-violence. He died in 1910.

bio|09-09|1901|Ανρί ντε Τουλούζ-Λωτρέκ|Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec|Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec was a French painter and poster artist. He depicted the nightlife of Paris, with the Moulin Rouge, and died young, at the age of 36.

bio|09-09|1941|Ντένις Ρίτσι|Dennis Ritchie|Dennis Ritchie was an American computer scientist. He created the C programming language and worked with Ken Thompson on the Unix operating system. He died in 2011.

bio|09-09|1949|Σουσίλο Μπάμπανγκ Γιουντχογιόνο|Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono|Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono is an Indonesian general and politician. He was president of Indonesia from 2004 to 2014, the first to be elected by direct vote.

bio|09-09|1976|Μάο Τσετούνγκ|Mao Zedong|Mao Zedong was a Chinese communist leader. He founded the People's Republic of China in 1949 and led the country until his death in 1976. His policies, such as the "Great Leap Forward" and the Cultural Revolution, caused great losses.

bio|09-09|1985|Λούκα Μόντριτς|Luka Modrić|Luka Modrić is a Croatian footballer who plays as a midfielder. He played for Real Madrid and Milan and led Croatia to the final of the 2018 World Cup. In the same year he won the Ballon d'Or.
bio|09-10|1659|Χένρι Πέρσελ|Henry Purcell|Henry Purcell was an English Baroque composer. He wrote the opera "Dido and Aeneas" and music for the theatre. He died young, in 1695.

bio|09-10|1797|Μαίρη Γουόλστονκραφτ|Mary Wollstonecraft|Mary Wollstonecraft was an English writer and a forerunner of feminism. In "A Vindication of the Rights of Woman" she demanded equal education for women. She died a few days after the birth of her daughter, Mary Shelley.

bio|09-10|1839|Τσαρλς Σάντερς Περς|Charles Sanders Peirce|Charles Sanders Peirce was an American philosopher, logician and scientist. He is considered the founder of pragmatism and developed semiotics. He died in 1914.

bio|09-10|1892|Άρθουρ Χόλι Κόμπτον|Arthur Holly Compton|Arthur Holly Compton was an American physicist. He discovered the Compton effect, which proved the particle nature of light, and in 1927 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1962.

bio|09-10|1898|Ελισάβετ|Elisabeth of Austria|Elisabeth, known as "Sisi", was Empress of Austria and Queen of Hungary, the wife of Franz Joseph. She was assassinated in 1898 in Geneva by the anarchist Luigi Lucheni.

bio|09-10|1933|Καρλ Λάγκερφελντ|Karl Lagerfeld|Karl Lagerfeld was a German fashion designer. For years he was the creative director of the Chanel house and he also designed for Fendi and his own label. He died in 2019.
bio|09-10|1960|Κόλιν Φερθ|Colin Firth|Colin Firth is an English actor. He won an Oscar for "The King's Speech" and became known as Mr Darcy in the television adaptation of "Pride and Prejudice".

bio|09-10|1975|Τζορτζ Τόμσον|George Paget Thomson|George Paget Thomson was an English physicist, the son of J. J. Thomson. He proved that electrons have a wave nature and in 1937 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1975.

bio|09-10|2025|Τσαρλς Τζέιμς Κερκ|Charlie Kirk|Charlie Kirk was an American conservative activist and commentator, the founder of the organisation Turning Point USA. He was assassinated on 10 September 2025 at an event at a university in Utah, at the age of 31.

bio|09-11|1823|Ντέηβιντ Ρικάρντο|David Ricardo|David Ricardo was an English economist of the classical school. He formulated the theory of comparative advantage in international trade. He died in 1823.

bio|09-11|1862|Ο. Χένρι|O. Henry|O. Henry, whose real name was William Sydney Porter, was an American short story writer. He became known for his unexpected endings, as in "The Gift of the Magi". He died in 1910.

bio|09-11|1885|Ντ. Χ. Λώρενς|D. H. Lawrence|D. H. Lawrence was an English writer. He wrote "Women in Love", "Sons and Lovers" and "Lady Chatterley's Lover", which was banned for years. He died in 1930.

bio|09-11|1917|Φερδινάντο Μάρκος|Ferdinand Marcos|Ferdinand Marcos was a Filipino politician. He governed the Philippines as president and dictator from 1965 to 1986, when he was overthrown after a popular uprising. He died in 1989 in Hawaii.

bio|09-11|1945|Φραντς Μπεκενμπάουερ|Franz Beckenbauer|Franz Beckenbauer was a German footballer, known as "the Kaiser". He won the World Cup as a player in 1974 and as a coach in 1990. He died in 2024.

bio|09-11|1948|Μοχάμεντ Αλί Τζίνα|Muhammad Ali Jinnah|Muhammad Ali Jinnah was the founder of Pakistan. He led the All-India Muslim League and became the country's first governor-general in 1947. He died in 1948.
bio|09-11|1965|Μπασάρ αλ Άσαντ|Bashar al-Assad|Bashar al-Assad is a Syrian politician. He was president of Syria from 2000 until late 2024, when he was overthrown after a long civil war.

bio|09-11|1971|Νικίτα Χρουστσόφ|Nikita Khrushchev|Nikita Khrushchev was a Soviet politician. He led the Soviet Union from 1953 to 1964 and in his speech of 1956 he condemned the crimes of Stalin. He was the leader during the Cuban Missile Crisis.

bio|09-11|1973|Σαλβαδόρ Αλιέντε|Salvador Allende|Salvador Allende was President of Chile. On 11 September 1973 General Pinochet's military junta overthrew his government, and he died in the presidential palace, La Moneda.

bio|09-12|1764|Ζαν Φιλίπ Ραμώ|Jean-Philippe Rameau|Jean-Philippe Rameau was a French composer and music theorist. He wrote operas, such as "Les Indes galantes", and the "Treatise on Harmony". He died in 1764.

bio|09-12|1897|Ιρέν Ζολιό-Κιουρί|Irène Joliot-Curie|Irène Joliot-Curie was a French physicist and chemist, the daughter of Marie and Pierre Curie. Together with her husband Frédéric she discovered artificial radioactivity, and in 1935 they were awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. She died in 1956.
bio|09-12|1913|Τζέσι Όουενς|Jesse Owens|Jesse Owens was an American athlete. He won four gold medals at the 1936 Olympic Games in Berlin, in the presence of Hitler. He died in 1980.
bio|09-12|1921|Στάνισλαβ Λεμ|Stanisław Lem|Stanisław Lem was a Polish science fiction writer. He wrote "Solaris" and the "Ijon Tichy" stories. He died in 2006.
bio|09-12|1973|Πολ Γουόκερ|Paul Walker|Paul Walker was an American actor. He became known through the "Fast and Furious" film series and was killed in a car accident in 2013, at the age of 40.

bio|09-12|1981|Εουτζένιο Μοντάλε|Eugenio Montale|Eugenio Montale was an Italian poet. He wrote the collection "Cuttlefish Bones" and in 1975 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1981.
bio|09-12|1986|Έμμυ Ρόσουμ|Emmy Rossum|Emmy Rossum is an American singer and actress. She became known for the film "The Phantom of the Opera" and for her album as a singer.
bio|09-12|1992|Άντονι Πέρκινς|Anthony Perkins|Anthony Perkins was an American actor. He became known as Norman Bates in Hitchcock's film "Psycho". He died in 1992.

bio|09-12|2003|Τζόνι Κας|Johnny Cash|Johnny Cash was an American country singer and songwriter. He became known with hits such as "Ring of Fire" and "Folsom Prison Blues", and he was called "the Man in Black". He died in 2003.

bio|09-13|1592|Μισέλ ντε Μονταίν|Michel de Montaigne|Michel de Montaigne was a French philosopher and writer. He created the essay form with his "Essays", in which he reflects on humanity and life. He died in 1592.

bio|09-13|1598|Φίλιππος Β΄|Philip II|Philip II was King of Spain from 1556 to 1598 and of Portugal from 1580. His empire was one of the largest in the world. His fleet was defeated by England in 1588.
bio|09-13|1660|Ντάνιελ Ντεφόε|Daniel Defoe|Daniel Defoe was an English writer and journalist. He wrote the novel "Robinson Crusoe" in 1719. He died in 1731.

bio|09-13|1872|Λούντβιχ Φόιερμπαχ|Ludwig Feuerbach|Ludwig Feuerbach died in 1872. He was a German philosopher, and his critique of religion, in the work "The Essence of Christianity", influenced Marx.
bio|09-13|1903|Κλοντέτ Κολμπέρ|Claudette Colbert|Claudette Colbert was born in 1903 in France. She was an American actress and won an Oscar for "It Happened One Night". She died in 1996.

bio|09-13|1916|Ρόαλντ Νταλ|Roald Dahl|Roald Dahl was a Welsh writer, born to Norwegian parents. He wrote children's books such as "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory", "Matilda" and "The BFG". He died in 1990.
bio|09-13|1989|Τόμας Μύλερ|Thomas Müller|Thomas Müller is a German footballer who plays as a forward. He played for Bayern Munich and won the 2014 World Cup.

bio|09-13|1996|Τούπακ Σακούρ|Tupac Shakur|Tupac Shakur was an American rapper and actor. He was one of the most important rappers of the 1990s. He was shot in Las Vegas and died in 1996, at the age of 25.
bio|09-14|1321|Δάντης Αλιγκέρι|Dante Alighieri|Dante Alighieri was an Italian poet from Florence. He wrote the "Divine Comedy", with Hell, Purgatory and Paradise. He died in Ravenna in 1321.
bio|09-14|1580|Φρανθίσκο δε Κεβέδο|Francisco de Quevedo|Francisco de Quevedo was a Spanish writer of the Golden Age. He wrote satirical works, such as "El Buscón", and poetry. He died in 1645.

bio|09-14|1769|Αλεξάντερ φον Χούμπολτ|Alexander von Humboldt|Alexander von Humboldt was a German naturalist and explorer. He travelled in Latin America and wrote "Cosmos". He is regarded as one of the pioneers of ecology and geography. He died in 1859.

bio|09-14|1901|Ουίλλιαμ ΜακΚίνλεϊ|William McKinley|William McKinley was the 25th president of the United States. He was shot on 6 September 1901 in Buffalo by an anarchist and died on 14 September. During his term the Spanish-American War took place.

bio|09-14|1927|Ισιδώρα Ντάνκαν|Isadora Duncan|Isadora Duncan was an American dancer and a pioneer of modern dance. Her dance was based on the movements of nature and on ancient Greece. She died in 1927 in Nice, when her long scarf became tangled in the wheel of a car.

bio|09-14|1937|Ρέντσο Πιάνο|Renzo Piano|Renzo Piano is an Italian architect. Together with Richard Rogers he designed the Centre Pompidou in Paris and, alone, the Shard building in London. In 1998 he was awarded the Pritzker Prize.

bio|09-14|1965|Ντμίτρι Μεντβέντεφ|Dmitry Medvedev|Dmitry Medvedev is a Russian politician. He was president of Russia from 2008 to 2012 and prime minister for several years, and he is deputy chairman of the Security Council.

bio|09-14|1982|Γκρέις Κέλι|Grace Kelly|Grace Kelly was an American actress. She won an Oscar for "The Country Girl" and in 1956 married Prince Rainier III of Monaco. She died in 1982 in a car accident.

bio|09-14|1983|Έιμι Γουάινχαουζ|Amy Winehouse|Amy Winehouse was born in 1983 in London. She was a singer with a jazz and soul voice and won several Grammy awards for "Back to Black". She died in 2011.

bio|09-15|1254|Μάρκο Πόλο|Marco Polo|Marco Polo was a Venetian merchant and explorer. He travelled in Asia and lived in China, and the account of his travels became very well known. The exact date of his birth is uncertain. He died in 1324.

bio|09-15|1613|Φρανσουά ντε Λα Ροσφουκώ|François de La Rochefoucauld|François de La Rochefoucauld was a French writer. He became known for the "Maxims", short sayings with a pessimistic view of human nature. He died in 1680.

bio|09-15|1789|Τζέιμς Φένιμορ Κούπερ|James Fenimore Cooper|James Fenimore Cooper was an American writer. He wrote "The Last of the Mohicans" and other novels about the frontier of America. He died in 1851.

bio|09-15|1890|Άγκαθα Κρίστι|Agatha Christie|Agatha Christie was an English writer of detective novels. She created the detectives Hercule Poirot and Miss Marple and wrote the play "The Mousetrap". She died in 1976.
